# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. PLACEMENT GAMES
Games where you place objects, numbers, or marks in cells

### A. Light/Illumination
- **Akari** - Place light bulbs that illuminate rows/columns

### B. Number Placement
- **Sudoku** - Place numbers 1-9 in rows, columns, and blocks
- **Nansuke** - Fill blank cells with numbers from a list
- **Makaro** - Fill cells with numbers based on directional arrow constraints
- **Ripple Effect** - Fill rooms with consecutive numbers starting from 1
- **Kurotto** - Color cells based on number constraints in circles

### C. Block/Shape Placement
- **Chained Block** - Fill cells to create numbered blocks in chains
- **Choco Banana** - Paint cells to form rectangles/squares
- **Evolomino** - Draw squares that progress along arrow paths
- **Five Cells** - Divide grid into blocks of exactly five cells
- **Fillomino** - Fill blocks with numbers matching block size
- **LITS** - Color four-cell tetrominoes in each region
- **Shikaku** - Divide grid into rectangles containing one number
- **Shakashaka** - Place triangles so white areas form rectangles/squares
- **Sashigane** - Divide grid into L-shaped blocks
- **Nuritwin** - Shade two equal-sized blocks per region

### D. Circle/Object Movement
- **Satogaeri** - Move circles so each country contains one
- **Yosenabe** - Move circles into gray areas with matching sums

---

## II. COLORING/SHADING GAMES
Games where you color or shade cells

### A. Black Cell Placement
- **Kurodoko** - Color cells black based on distance constraints
- **Hitori** - Color cells to eliminate duplicate numbers in rows/columns
- **Nurikabe** - Color cells to create continuous black wall with white regions
- **Usowan** - Color cells based on neighbor count (with one wrong number per region)
- **Sto-stone** - Color cells that "drop" to fill bottom half of grid
- **Tilepaint** - Color tiles based on diagonal line constraints
- **Norinori** - Color two black squares per region

### B. Mixed Coloring
- **Heyawake** - Paint cells in rooms with connectivity constraints
- **Nurimeizu** - Paint cells to create maze from S to G
- **Nurimisaki** - Color cells with white "promontory" constraints
- **Double Choco** - Divide blocks into matching white/gray cell pairs

---

## III. LINE-DRAWING GAMES
Games where you draw lines to form loops or paths

### A. Single Loop Games
- **Dotchi-Loop** - Draw loop through white circles with turn constraints
- **Masyu** - Draw loop with constraints at white/black circles
- **Slitherlink** - Connect dots to form loop with number constraints
- **Nagareru** - Draw loop following arrow directions with wind constraints
- **Suraromu** - Draw loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing gates
- **Moon-or-Sun** - Draw loop alternating between moon/sun cells per room
- **Mid-loop** - Draw loop with black circles as midpoints
- **Yajilin** - Draw loop avoiding black cells indicated by arrows

### B. Path/Connection Games
- **Numberlink** - Connect pairs of same numbers with continuous lines
- **Hashiwokakero** - Connect islands with bridges matching numbers
- **Pencils** - Draw lines from pencil tips using length numbers

---

## IV. DIVISION/PARTITIONING GAMES
Games where you divide the grid into regions

### A. Region Division
- **Fillomino** - Divide into blocks matching their number values
- **Five Cells** - Divide into blocks of exactly five cells
- **Shikaku** - Divide into rectangles, each containing one number
- **Sashigane** - Divide into L-shaped blocks

### B. Block Pairing
- **Double Choco** - Divide into blocks with matching white/gray pairs
- **Nuritwin** - Divide into regions with two equal-sized shaded blocks

---

## V. HYBRID GAMES
Games combining multiple mechanics

- **Chained Block** - Coloring + block division with chain connectivity
- **Choco Banana** - Coloring + rectangle formation
- **Evolomino** - Placement + path following with progression
- **Hebi** - Number placement + snake connectivity constraints
- **Juosan** - Filling cells with marks + territory constraints
- **LITS** - Coloring + tetromino placement + connectivity
- **Ripple Effect** - Number placement + room-based constraints

---

## VI. CONSTRAINT TYPES (Cross-cutting)

**Connectivity Requirements:**
- Continuous networks (Akari, Hitori, Nurikabe, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, Numberlink, Hashiwokakero)

**Directional/Arrow Constraints:**
- Makaro, Nagareru, Yajilin, Evolomino, Sashigane, Pencils

**Room/Region-Based Rules:**
- Makaro, Ripple Effect, Heyawake, Moon-or-Sun, Norinori, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan

**Symmetry/Matching Constraints:**
- Double Choco, Nuritwin, Shakashaka
